proposals.description: Governs the economic exchange and physical transfer of items between entities, handling bartering, gifting, looting, and need-based acquisition.

specification.name: ResourceTransactionSystem
specification.description: Governs the economic exchange and physical transfer of items between entities, handling bartering, gifting, looting, and need-based acquisition.
specification.logic: 1. Identify Agents with active 'Acquire' Goals or critical Needs (e.g., high Hunger requiring food). 2. Scan the local Room or adjacent GridPositions for entities (Agents or Containers) holding the required Item in their Inventory. 3. Calculate 'Willingness to Trade' based on the Provider's Personality (Generosity/Greed) and the Receiver's Desperation (Need level). 4. If conditions are met (consensual trade or unobserved theft), execute the transfer: Remove Item from Provider's Inventory and add to Receiver's Inventory. 5. If a reciprocal value is required (barter), identifying a matching item of value in the Receiver's Inventory and transfer it to the Provider. 6. Generate a Memory for involved Agents describing the nature of the transaction (Fair Trade, Charity, or Theft). 7. Mark the 'Acquire' Goal as complete if successful.

proposals.rationale: Currently, agents have items and inventories but no mechanism to exchange them. A transaction system would allow agents to fulfill their 'Needs' through trade, transforming the static 'Goal: 0' state into a dynamic flow of goods between specialized roles like the Baker, Blacksmith, and Farmers.

proposals.description: Synthesizes an agent's biological Needs, psychological Personality, and moral Beliefs to manufacture or update actionable Goals.

specification.name: MotivationGenerator
specification.description: Synthesizes an agent's biological Needs, psychological Personality, and moral Beliefs to manufacture or update actionable Goals.
specification.logic: 1. Iterate through all entities possessing Agent, Needs, Personality, and Mind components. 2. Calculate the 'Urgency' score for each Need (e.g., Hunger, Energy, Social) based on current values versus thresholds. 3. Apply Personality modifiers to these scores (e.g., a 'Diligent' agent creates work goals sooner; a 'Stoic' agent suppresses pain/comfort needs). 4. Consult Belief components to whitelist or blacklist potential methods of satisfying needs (e.g., an 'Honest' agent will not generate a 'Steal' goal to satisfy 'Money' need). 5. If specific Beliefs dictate proactive behavior (e.g., 'Devout'), generate ritualistic Goals when survival Needs are low. 6. Compare calculated priorities against the current list of Goals in the Mind. 7. If a new high-priority driver is found, instantiate a new Goal component with specific success conditions. 8. Re-sort the agent's Goal queue, placing the highest weighted motivation at the front. 9. Mark Goals associated with satisfied Needs as complete for removal.

proposals.rationale: Currently, all 17 agents have 0 goals. Without a system to drive desire and intent, the NarrativeEvents system lacks the friction necessary to create a story. A MotivationGenerator will ensure agents are proactive rather than reactive.

proposals.name: GoalInceptionSystem
proposals.description: Evaluates agent needs, personality traits, and environmental context to generate and prioritize actionable goals within the agent's mind.

specification.name: GoalInceptionSystem
specification.description: Evaluates agent needs, personality traits, and environmental context to generate and prioritize actionable goals within the agent's mind.
specification.logic: 1. Iterate through all entities possessing Agent, Mind, and Needs components. 2. Assess current Needs values; if Hunger, Thirst, or Energy cross critical thresholds (e.g., > 70%), generate candidate survival goals. 3. Cross-reference recent Memory entries and active Beliefs to generate context-sensitive goals (e.g., 'Flee' if a threat is remembered nearby). 4. Apply Personality multipliers to candidate goal scores (e.g., a 'Bravery' trait lowers the score of 'Flee' goals and raises 'Defend' goals). 5. Compare the highest-scoring candidate goal against the currently active Goal in the Mind component. 6. If the new candidate score exceeds the current goal's priority by a defined margin, instantiate the new Goal and inject it into the Mind's goal queue. 7. Emit a 'goal_formed' event.

proposals.rationale: Currently, all 17 agents have 0 active goals. A GoalInceptionSystem is required to parse an agent's 'Needs', 'Personality', and 'Beliefs' to generate autonomous objectives, transitioning the simulation from a static state to an active narrative.

proposals.description: Transforms resource depletion into urgent economic objectives by automatically generating high-value acquisition mandates when critical stock falls below safety margins.

proposals.rationale: Currently, all 17 agents have 0 active goals despite having a 'Needs' component. This rule would bridge the 'Needs' state with the 'GoalInceptionSystem', forcing agents to generate goals (e.g., 'Acquire Food', 'Earn Currency') when their status effects or needs fall below a threshold. This is the primary engine for economic activity.

proposals.name: MetabolicDegradationSystem
proposals.description: Governs the biological entropy of living agents by decreasing vital need statistics over time and applying physiological penalties or health reduction when thresholds are breached.

specification.name: MetabolicDegradationSystem
specification.description: Governs the biological entropy of living agents by decreasing vital need statistics over time and applying physiological penalties or health reduction when thresholds are breached.
specification.logic: 1. Iterate through all entities possessing 'Agent' and 'Needs' components. 2. Calculate metabolic burn rate: Base rate + modifier if 'InCombat' is present. 3. Decrement 'Needs' values (Hunger, Thirst, Rest) by the calculated rate. 4. Evaluate Thresholds: If a specific need drops below 20%, instantiate and attach a corresponding negative 'StatusEffect' (e.g., 'Weakened', 'Dehydrated'). 5. Critical Failure: If a need reaches 0, deduct value from 'Health' component (Starvation damage). 6. Recovery: If a need rises above 20%, remove the associated negative 'StatusEffect'. 7. If 'Health' reaches 0 due to metabolic decay, flag agent for death processing.

proposals.rationale: For a ResourceTransactionSystem to be meaningful, resources must be finite and consumable. This system would ensure that items (like Ada's bread) are removed from the simulation upon use and that agent 'Needs' decay over time. Without consumption, the market will inevitably reach a point of inventory saturation and total stagnation.

specification.description: Orchestrates the invisible hand of the market by dynamically calculating the perceived value of goods based on local scarcity, agent desperation, and aggregate supply.
specification.logic: 1. Iterate through active Rooms to identify local market clusters. 2. For each Room, aggregate the total 'Supply' of specific Items held in Agent Inventories. 3. Calculate 'Demand' by summing the intensity of relevant Agent Needs and active Goals requiring those Items. 4. Compute a 'Local Value Modifier' (Demand / Supply) for each commodity. 5. Update the Belief component of each Agent in the Room to reflect the new perceived value of the Item (e.g., creating a belief that 'Water is worth 50 gold' during a drought). 6. Adjust individual valuation thresholds based on Personality (e.g., greedy agents inflate sell prices, desperate agents accept higher buy prices).

proposals.rationale: While 'MarketExchange' exists, there is no mechanism to determine the fluctuating value of goods based on scarcity or urgency. A PriceDiscoverySystem would allow agents like Greta the Merchant and Bjorn the Blacksmith to adjust prices based on the 'DemandManifestationSystem', creating economic tension and profit motives.

proposals.description: Calculates the dynamic exchange value of items by weighing local scarcity (Inventory) against agent desperation (Needs) and disposition (Personality), establishing the perceived worth (Belief) prior to transaction.

specification.name: PriceDiscoverySystem
specification.description: Calculates the dynamic exchange value of items by weighing local scarcity (Inventory) against agent desperation (Needs) and disposition (Personality), establishing the perceived worth (Belief) prior to transaction.
specification.logic: 1. Identify Agents actively seeking to buy or sell, or those responding to a `trade_initiated` trigger. 2. For Sellers: specific `Item` value is calculated by checking `Inventory` count (Scarcity Factor) inversely correlated to price, then modified by the agent's current `Needs` (Desperation Factor determines if they sell cheap for quick relief or hold for high value). 3. For Buyers: Determine value by checking how significantly an `Item` satisfies current high `Needs` (Utility Factor). 4. Apply `Personality` traits as modifiers (e.g., 'Greedy' increases sell margin/decreases buy offer; 'Generous' relaxes margins). 5. Cross-reference `Memory` for past transaction prices to establish an anchor point. 6. Update the Agent's `Belief` component with a specific 'perceived_value' for the target item, setting the floor or ceiling for the `MarketExchange` system.

proposals.rationale: While 'MarketExchange' exists, there is no mechanism to translate 'DemandManifestation' and 'MetabolicDegradation' into fluctuating values. A Price Discovery system would adjust the cost of items based on local scarcity and inventory levels, creating the 'profit motive' necessary to trigger the MotivationGenerator.

proposals.description: Monitors the simulation for narrative stagnation and injects disruptive external events to disturb the equilibrium of Agents, forcing them to form new reactionary goals and beliefs.

specification.name: IncitingIncidentGenerator
specification.description: Monitors the simulation for narrative stagnation and injects disruptive external events to disturb the equilibrium of Agents, forcing them to form new reactionary goals and beliefs.
specification.logic: 1. Scan all Agents possessing a Mind and Personality component. 2. Calculate a 'DramaScore' for each agent based on the recency of traumatic entries in their Memory and current Goal urgency (low urgency + old memories = high stagnation). 3. Identify pairs of agents with opposing Personality traits or geographic proximity but no active interaction. 4. If stagnation exceeds threshold, generate a specific Inciting Incident archetype (e.g., 'Missing Item', 'Perceived Slight', 'Resource Scarcity Rumor'). 5. For 'Missing Item', move an Item from the Agent's Inventory to a hidden location or another Agent's inventory, then inject a 'Discovery' Memory of the loss. 6. For 'Perceived Slight', inject a negative Belief regarding a target Agent tailored to the subject's Personality (e.g., a paranoid agent believes they are being watched). 7. For 'Resource Scarcity', modify a Belief about the abundance of a specific item in the local GridPosition. 8. Immediately trigger the GoalInceptionSystem to convert the new Memory/Belief into an actionable Goal (e.g., 'Recover Item', 'Confront Rival').

proposals.rationale: Currently, all 17 agents have 0 active goals despite the presence of a GoalInceptionSystem. The simulation lacks a 'spark' to convert metabolic and social needs into narrative action. A DramaEngine would inject external pressures or 'Inciting Incidents' (e.g., a theft, a miracle, a sudden shortage) that force agents to adopt contrasting goals.

proposals.description: Translates abstract agent goals into concrete state changes, handling physical movement, resource utilization, and interaction outcomes.

specification.name: ActionExecutionSystem
specification.description: Translates abstract agent goals into concrete state changes, handling physical movement, resource utilization, and interaction outcomes.
specification.logic: 1. Identify Agents with an active, unsatisfied Goal. 2. Determine the physical requirements of the Goal (e.g., reach a location, acquire an item, interact with a target). 3. If the Agent is not at the required Position/GridPosition, calculate the path and update GridPosition towards the target. 4. If the Agent is at the target location, execute the interaction: if 'Consumption', remove Item from Inventory and restore Needs; if 'Combat', calculate damage using CombatStats and reduce target Health; if 'Acquisition', transfer Item to Inventory. 5. Apply energy costs to Agent Needs for movement and exertion. 6. If the action satisfies the Goal criteria, mark the Goal as complete. 7. Emit events based on the outcome (success/failure).

proposals.rationale: Currently, agents have goals (0) and minds, but no mechanism to translate internal desires into world-state changes. This system would bridge the gap between GoalInception and physical/social outcomes, allowing agents to perform tasks like crafting, moving, or conversing.

Updates Beliefs regarding 'Creditworthiness' or 'Trust' for specific target agents based on repayment history. 5. If a debt remains unpaid beyond a threshold, the creditor's Belief shifts from 'Ally' to 'Defaulter', triggering a Goal to 'Extract Value' or 'Slander Reputation'.

proposals.rationale: With a PriceDiscoverySystem already in place, the simulation needs a way to handle liquidity. Not every transaction can be a direct barter; a ledger allows for emergent behaviors like predatory lending, indentured servitude, or communal gratitude, adding depth to the SocialDynamics.

specification.logic: 1. Iterate through populated Rooms to calculate a 'Local Tension Index' derived from agent density, conflicting Beliefs, and aggregate Needs deprivation. 2. If the index indicates stagnation (low activity/conflict), apply 'Atmospheric Pressure': inject 'Paranoid' or 'Urgent' Thoughts into Minds and temporarily increase the decay rate of Needs to force movement or competition. 3. If the index reaches a critical threshold, trigger 'Breaking Point': override current lower-priority Goals with immediate survival or confrontation Goals based on agent Personality (e.g., Aggressive agents seek conflict, Neurotic agents flee). 4. Implant a 'Tense Atmosphere' Memory in local agents to synchronize their perception of the escalation.

proposals.rationale: Currently, all agents have 0 goals and neutral arousal, indicating a state of narrative stasis. This system would monitor 'Boredom' or 'Stagnation' metrics and inject 'Inciting Incidents' (external shocks or internal desires) to force agents into the GoalInceptionSystem.

proposals.name: UtilityValuationSystem
proposals.description: Calculates the subjective utility of items and actions for an Agent based on their current biological Needs, active Goals, and Personality traits. It determines not what an item costs in the market, but what it is worth to the specific individual at that moment, driving trade decisions and consumption.

specification.name: UtilityValuationSystem
specification.description: Calculates the subjective utility of items and actions for an Agent based on their current biological Needs, active Goals, and Personality traits. It determines not what an item costs in the market, but what it is worth to the specific individual at that moment, driving trade decisions and consumption.
specification.logic: 1. Iterate through agents with Needs and Personality components. 2. Establish 'Need Urgency' derived from current Need deficits (e.g., high Hunger creates high demand for Food category items). 3. Evaluate items in the Agent's Inventory and immediate GridPosition. 4. Calculate a 'Utility Score' for each item: Base Utility + (Need Reduction * Urgency) + (Goal Relevance Multiplier). 5. Apply Personality modifiers (e.g., a 'Materialistic' agent applies a bonus multiplier to high-rarity items; a 'Cautious' agent values Weapons higher). 6. Store or update a Belief component linked to the Item, recording its 'SubjectiveValue'. 7. Compare 'SubjectiveValue' against known 'MarketPrice' in Memory to determine if the agent considers the item a 'Surplus' (sellable) or a 'Necessity' (hoardable).

proposals.rationale: While the simulation has 'PriceDiscovery', agents currently lack a subjective way to value items. This system would calculate an agent's 'Willingness to Pay' based on their current 'Needs', 'Personality', and 'Inventory' levels, turning static items into dynamic assets.

proposals.rationale: Currently, agents exist in rooms but do not 'own' the means of production (e.g., Bjorn owning the Forge). Ownership creates a basis for rent, exclusive production rights, and territorial conflict, which are the bedrock of a complex economy.

proposals.description: Simulates the economic interface with the outside world, managing the influx of foreign goods and the export of local surplus via caravans and port connections.

specification.name: MacroTradeSystem
specification.description: Simulates the economic interface with the outside world, managing the influx of foreign goods and the export of local surplus via caravans and port connections.
specification.logic: 1. Scan for Agents located in designated 'Entry' Rooms (Gates/Docks) acting as trade liaisons. 2. Calculate 'External Market' volatility to determine current import availability and export demand. 3. Import Phase: Generate items representing outside goods (rare resources, luxury items) and add them to the liaison's Inventory. 4. Export Phase: Identify surplus items in the liaison's Inventory (local production), remove them, and replace with currency based on external demand. 5. Trigger a 'caravan_arrival' event to notify local Agents that new stock is available.

proposals.rationale: A closed loop of 17 agents will eventually reach a stagnant equilibrium. An external trade system introduces 'shocks'—new currency influxes or demands for local exports—that force the PriceDiscoverySystem to react to global rather than just local scarcity.

action.content: Do you not feel it, Mira? The chill in the air that has nothing to do with the morning mist? It is the chill of forgetting. Of turning away from the true reverence, the true debt we owe the Harvest Mother.

data.insight: My desire to restore the old ways stems from a deeper need for connection and control, masked by bitterness. The community's preparations for the harvest festival, while 'shallow' in my eyes, still hold a pull, suggesting that change is inevitable, and perhaps I should focus on guiding that change rather than resisting it entirely. The stranger and the unusual things I've noticed could represent either allies or threats to this potential guidance.

specification.description: Manages the generation and lifecycle of external disasters and systemic shocks that disrupt agent equilibrium and force adaptation.
specification.logic: 1. Monitors simulation stability metric; if equilibrium persists beyond threshold, probability of crisis increases. 2. Triggers crisis event (Wildfire, Plague, or Blight) based on biome data. 3. For Wildfire: Selects Room cluster, modifies Description to 'Scorched', destroys organic Items in Inventory, applies 'Burning' StatusEffect and direct Health damage to Agents present. 4. proposals.description: Evaluates agent needs, inventory surpluses, and subjective value beliefs to formulate transactional goals. It translates biological scarcity and material abundance into market demand and supply pressures.

specification.name: EconomicIncentiveGenerator
specification.description: Evaluates agent needs, inventory surpluses, and subjective value beliefs to formulate transactional goals. It translates biological scarcity and material abundance into market demand and supply pressures.
specification.logic: 1. Scarcity Evaluation: Iterates through Agent Needs (e.g., Hunger). If a Need is below a critical threshold and the relevant consumable Item is absent from Inventory, calculates a 'Desperation' score. 2. Surplus Identification: Scans Inventory for Items exceeding a subjective retention threshold defined in Beliefs. Marks these items as 'Liquidatable'. 3. Valuation Heuristic: Consults Beliefs regarding perceived item value and local availability. 4. Incentive Synthesis: If Desperation is high, creates a Goal to 'Acquire [Item]' via trade or labor. If Surplus is high, creates a Goal to 'Sell [Item]' to convert to value. 5. Opportunity Injection: If the Agent remembers (Memory) a price disparity for an item between two locations, and possesses said item, creates a speculative Goal for arbitrage.

proposals.rationale: Currently, all 17 agents have 0 goals and a neutral arousal of 0.50. While systems for transaction and production exist, there is no engine translating 'Needs' and 'MetabolicDegradation' into actionable economic 'Goals'. This system would bridge that gap, forcing agents to engage with the MarketExchange to survive or prosper.
